content_html:
Blinds and shades can often be cleaned while installed if the method matches the material and mechanism. Start by removing dry dust, then spot-clean with the minimum moisture needed and avoid soaking cords, motors, or fabrics marked for professional cleaning only. Technique differs for aluminum, wood, PVC, and fabric shades.

Remove dust first with gentle vacuuming or microfiber

Close slats in one direction and work from top to bottom, then reverse them if the design allows. On fabric shades, use an upholstery attachment at low suction so pleats are not distorted.

Match moisture to the material

polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and aluminum usually tolerate a damp cloth better than wood or delicate fabrics. Wring the cloth well and test at an edge. Do not spray directly toward mechanisms, headrails, or motorized components.

Spot-clean stains without soaking

Use a compatible mild cleaner and blot from the edge toward the center on fabrics to reduce rings. If the label calls for dry cleaning or color transfers to the cloth, stop wet cleaning.

Clean cords and chains with the system stationary

Wipe accessible cords or chains with a barely damp cloth without pulling on the mechanism. If a chain jams, a cord is frayed, or a motorized shade fails, do not use cleaning as a reason to dismantle a loaded headrail.

faq.answer: Close slats in one direction and work from top to bottom, then reverse them if the design allows. On fabric shades, use an upholstery attachment at low suction so pleats are not distorted.

faq.question: Can wood and PVC blinds be cleaned the same way?
faq.answer: polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and aluminum usually tolerate a damp cloth better than wood or delicate fabrics. Wring the cloth well and test at an edge. Do not spray directly toward mechanisms, headrails, or motorized components.

faq.question: When should I stop wet-cleaning a fabric shade?
faq.answer: Use a compatible mild cleaner and blot from the edge toward the center on fabrics to reduce rings. If the label calls for dry cleaning or color transfers to the cloth, stop wet cleaning.
